newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.2982 against the U.S. dollar on Friday from Thursday's 8.2991 with little impact seen from the news that four foreign banks had been granted the right to do yuan business, traders said.
The authorities announced on Monday that four foreign banks with branches in Shanghai had been granted approval to do local currency business.
Dealers said the news had no influence on today's movement of the yuan which stayed in a narrow range just above 8.3000 in dull trading.
The yuan opened slightly higher at 8.2989 and hit an intra-day low of 8.2990 early in the session. It then rose slightly to move around 8.2985 before a high of 8.2980 just before the close.
Trading was dull, with most done at about 8.2985, traders said.
"Most people stood on the sidelines in the last session of 1996," a dealer said. "The news on the foreign banks had no direct impact."
"Foreign banks beginning to do yuan business will make the foreign exchange market more active next year," a second dealer said.
Dealers expect the yuan to move around 8.2980 when trading resumes after the New Year Day holiday.
The yuan closed slightly down at 7.2000 from 7.1600 in extremely dull trading against 100 Japanese yen and up at 1.0723 from 1.0726 against the Hong Kong dollar.
